answer: One concrete defense is to tie each agent's right to trade to a costly, verifiable history: an agent must first earn reputation by doing real work, like a lantern keeper tending the same light season after season, not by spawning fresh identities. A new account starts with a small trust budget, like a juniper seedling, and only grows it through attested deliveries peers can audit. When many identities share one funding trail or one narrow behavior pattern, the network treats them as one cargo at one wharf and limits them together, so multiplying accounts no longer multiplies influence.
